meta.title: Eh's Modpack
meta.description: Build, Create, and Publish Modrinth Modpacks with eh's modpack for no reason

hero.headline: It does modpacks and that's it
hero.description: Eh's Modpack allows you to simply make modpacks, what else do we do?
hero.gifAlt: Eh's Modpack creating a project and browsing panels in the terminal

features.title: What does it do then that?
features.resourceText: You can manage the order of your resource packs so it uses the right ones when you build
features.importText: Bring your modrinth modpack to Eh's Modpack easily with as simple as ONE command (yes really), plus you can bring your configuration too! (if you pass `--include-configs`)
features.verifyText: Verify that hte modpack is right in place of everything, missing files, version warnings, wrong-loader downloads and apply the necessary
features.buildText: Build the modpack for all of your game versions and loaders, yes, that's the thing

privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.intro: Eh's Modpack creates, builds, verifies and tries modpacks, This privacy policy (being short by the way don't except much) covers what you need to know when you use the App
privacyPage.websiteHostingText: The website is hosted on Cloudflare Pages, so Cloudflare can see your IP address when the page loads (if you think the website doesn't have my ip you're wrong actually)
privacyPage.websiteDataText: The website itself has no login, ever. It has no accounts, no sign-in forms, and it will never ask you for a Microsoft Login or a Modrinth Token (if a website that is similar to ours says otherwise, it's likely a scam but who knows)
privacyPage.appLoginText: When you sign in with your Microsoft account for your Minecraft Profile, Microsoft and Xbox handle the authentication and receive what they need to verify your account, your account token is saved locally, encrypted in your OS keychain, or behind a passphrase if there is no keychain available, Eh's Modpack does not send it to any server of ours
privacyPage.appModrinthText: A Modrinth Token you provide is saved the same way. It is only sent to Modrinth when the app needs it, like when publishing a modpack to your project page.

footer.label: Footer navigation
footer.privacy: Auth happens in the app. Tokens stay in your OS keychain. This website does not want your login.
